completion_gate: The baseline map covers endomorphism-ring/path-finding, CSIDH/hidden-shift, CGL, and the SIDH-break lesson, with survivors vs broken schemes separated.
The candidate is deduplicated against the cited knowledge spine and known SIDH attacks.
The mechanism has explicit assumptions, predictions, full-cost boundary, and one cheap falsification gate — or the report returns NO_ADMISSIBLE_NEXT_MECHANISM with the residual open question named.
constraints: Academic defensive literature research only; no operational attacks.
Separate established literature, derivation, speculation, and proposed tests.
SIDH/SIKE torsion-image key recovery is a closed known attack — not a novelty target.
Do not reuse RQ-ISO-001 ordinary-curve Semaev-neighbor scope.
Charge preprocessing, memory, oracles, quantum queries, and verification.
Cite primary sources with stable URLs and record access dates where tools permit.
Make no breakthrough claim and change no official state.
inputs: The persistent goal and research question
Existing knowledge spine KN-LIT-062..079, KN-TECH-024..029, KN-OPEN-013..015
handoff.objective: Map the post-SIDH-break supersingular-isogeny cryptanalytic baseline and produce one novelty-screened, falsifiable algorithmic candidate against a surviving hardness assumption.
handoff.uncertainty_reduced: Whether a concrete mechanism beyond rediscovering the SIDH torsion-image attack or estimator retuning plausibly changes the cost of a surviving supersingular problem.

dispatches.title: Map and generate supersingular-isogeny cryptanalytic mechanisms

objective: Map surviving supersingular-isogeny attack baselines after the SIDH break, propose one falsifiable algorithmic mechanism against a survivor, and independently red-team it before experiment design.
